question: According to India's National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS), what is the 24-hour mean concentration limit for PM2.5?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: 15 µg/m³ is the WHO 2021 guideline, not the Indian NAAQS standard.
Correct. NAAQS 2009 sets the 24-hour PM2.5 standard at 60 µg/m³ for India.
100 µg/m³ is the 24-hour NAAQS limit for PM10, not PM2.5.
This exceeds both Indian and international standards for fine particulate matter.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review NAAQS 2009. India's 24-hour PM2.5 limit is 60 µg/m³ (annual 40 µg/m³); WHO 2021 guidelines are stricter at 15 µg/m³.
Well done! India's NAAQS 24-hour PM2.5 standard is 60 µg/m³, considerably more lenient than WHO guidelines, reflecting feasibility constraints.
